record.original_question: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite triangle-free graph with m edges has the largest spectral radius? Equivalently, among all non-bipartite graphs G with m edges and no C_3 subgraph, determine the extremal graph maximizing lambda(G).

evidence.quote: Problem 3 (Zhai and Shu [45], 2022). For even m, what is the extremal graph attaining the maximum spectral radius over all C3-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a simple graph with adjacency matrix $A(G)$, and let $\lambda(G)$ denote its spectral radius (the largest eigenvalue of $A(G)$). A graph is called triangle-free (or $C_3$-free) if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices, and bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two independent sets. Let $m$ be a positive even integer. Among all non-bipartite, triangle-free graphs $G$ with exactly $m$ edges, determine the maximum value of $\lambda(G)$ and characterize all graphs that attain this maximum.
artifact.category_tag: Spectral graph theory / extremal spectral radius
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Zhai and Shu in 2022 for the even-edge case, has been resolved. A paper in the Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (v31i1p52) characterizes three kinds of spectral extremal graphs among triangle-free non-bipartite graphs of even size, providing the sharp bound and extremal graphs.

status_evidence.title: A Spectral Extremal Problem on Non-Bipartite Triangle-Free Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: characterize three kinds of spectral extremal graphs over all triangle-free non-bipartite graphs with even size
status_evidence.claim: The even-m case of the Zhai-Shu problem has been solved by characterizing three families of extremal graphs.

status_evidence.title: The Maximum Spectral Radius of Non-Bipartite Graphs Forbidding Short Odd Cycles
status_evidence.snippet: Zhai and Shu's bound is tight only when m is odd; the even case was left open.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that Zhai-Shu's original bound was sharp only for odd m, motivating the even-m problem.
